TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURE REVIEW: DISTRIBUTED EVENT BUS SCALING
Document Version: 3.4.0
Status: Approved

OVERVIEW:
This architecture document outlines the migration of the core real-time telemetry pipeline to Apache Kafka and Redis cluster caching.
The target workload requires handling 450,000 QPS with sustained P99 latency below 15ms and P99.9 latency below 35ms.

KEY ARCHITECTURAL DECISIONS:
1. Message Ingestion & Streaming:
   - Deploy Apache Kafka clusters across three availability zones in AWS us-west-2.
   - Configure topic partition replication factor to 3 with min.insync.replicas set to 2.
   - Standardize payload serialization on Protocol Buffers over gRPC and HTTP/2.

2. Caching & State Management:
   - Utilize a distributed Redis cluster with master-replica failover via Raft consensus.
   - Memory eviction policy set to volatile-lru with maximum heap allocation of 64GB per node.
   - Fallback persistent storage anchored on Apache Cassandra with SSTable compaction.

3. Observability & Network Tracing:
   - Deploy eBPF kernel probes for zero-overhead socket lifecycle monitoring on Linux kernels 6.1+.
   - Metrics scrape interval set to 10 seconds via Prometheus with Alertmanager notification routing.
   - Encrypt all inter-pod traffic with TLS 1.3 mutual authentication (mTLS).
